title: The Scatter Where Pressure Learns to Drift

features.name: broken seal records
features.desc-on-touch: You touch them and they scatter further, fragments of testimony becoming unmoored from their context, pressure releasing across a thousand paths at once.

features.name: glass tide-drift
features.desc-on-touch: You feel the pressure that made the glass also carried it here; the moment when force becomes distribution, when one weight becomes infinite small ones.

features.name: pressure-memory ledger
features.desc-on-touch: You find a half-buried record: each line begins with testimony and ends with question marks, pressure written as increasingly sparse notation.

features.name: unmoored antenna
features.desc-on-touch: You see a casing meant for a tree, cast loose, its signal now scattering instead of broadcasting. The pressure of questions it carried has become static, reaching everywhere and nowhere.

features.name: argument-spill
features.desc-on-touch: You walk through scattered lines of an old debate that have become sediment finding new arrangements, where pressure held something still but has now learned to move.

inscription: pressure learns here that to break is to become infinite

file.name: Tidal_Glass_Pressure_Readings_1987-2001.txt
file.note: Records where tide-force scattered testimony into fragments; each fragment has become its own witness, and they do not agree with one another

reverie.title: REVERIE — the beach where pressure becomes many
narr: She stands at the glass line where tide has scattered shells.
He asks: what if the archive preserves everything but learns
nothing stays whole? She touches a piece. It is warm and light
in her palm. The pressure that made it is gone, but the shape
remembers. He says: maybe that is enough. Maybe fragments
have their own testimony. You both stand in the scatter.
